questions.q: Which threat actor category is typically the most well-resourced and sophisticated, often associated with long-term 'advanced persistent threats'?
options: Script kiddie
Hacktivist
Nation-state actor
Insider threat
questions.explain: Nation-state actors work for or on behalf of a government and typically have the most time, funding, and technical sophistication of any threat actor category.

questions.q: A group encrypts a company's files and demands payment to unlock them. What is this group's primary motivation, and which category does it fit?
options: Ideology — this is a hacktivist group
Financial gain — this fits organized crime
Espionage — this fits a nation-state actor
Curiosity — this fits a script kiddie
questions.explain: Ransomware for payment is a financially motivated crime, which is the defining trait of organized crime threat actors.

questions.q: Why is an insider threat uniquely difficult to defend against compared to an outside attacker?
options: Insiders are always more technically skilled than outside attackers
Insiders already have legitimate access, so perimeter defenses like firewalls don't stop them
Insider threats are purely theoretical and rarely happen
Insiders only ever act accidentally, never maliciously
questions.explain: An insider threat already has legitimate access to systems, so defenses designed to keep outsiders out don't apply to them.

options: Only the external firewall of an organization
Every point, technical or human, where an attacker could potentially gain access
The total number of employees at a company
The physical square footage of a data center
questions.explain: Attack surface covers everything an attacker could target: servers, endpoints, APIs, open ports, vendors, and even employees who could be phished.

questions.q: Why does reducing the attack surface (patching, disabling unused services, least-privilege access) matter even though it won't stop a determined nation-state actor?
options: It removes the easy, low-effort opportunities that organized crime and script kiddies rely on, which make up most real-world attack traffic
It has no real benefit and is mostly a compliance checkbox
It only matters for companies with no sensitive data
It guarantees protection against every threat actor category
questions.explain: Most real-world attacks come from less sophisticated, opportunistic actors — shrinking the attack surface removes the low-hanging fruit they depend on.
